extracted.intended_audience: general TED audience; internet users, communicators, and policymakers concerned about personalization and democracy
extracted.subtask_description: A short public-facing TED Talk arguing that algorithmic personalization (in news and search) creates 'filter bubbles' that limit exposure to challenging information and harm democratic discourse. The page summarizes the talk's thesis for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure to information that challenges or broadens worldview
rubrics_metrics.description: We get trapped in a 'filter bubble' and don't get exposed to information that could challenge or broaden our worldview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is framed as the central problem: tailoring of services (including news and search results) to personal tastes reduces users' exposure to diverse or challenging information. The page uses this statement to justify concern about personalization's social effects; no prescriptive implementation details are given here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive personalization that narrows experience
rubrics_metrics.description: As web companies strive to tailor their services (including news and search results) to our personal tastes, there's a dangerous unintended consequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit evaluative criterion for web services: weigh benefits of tailoring against the unintended consequence of narrowing users' informational environments. Example signals mentioned are tailored news and search results; the page positions this narrowing as a negative outcome to be avoided or mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate platforms for impact on democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Eli Pariser argues powerfully that this will ultimately prove to be bad for us and bad for democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to assess information systems not just for user engagement or personalization quality, but for their broader civic and democratic effects. The page emphasizes democratic harm as a key evaluative dimension; no scoring rubric is provided, but democratic impact is presented as a decisive negative consequence.
